html:
The Argentine great depression of 1998 to 2002 was a deep economic crisis in Argentina that peaked in December 2001 with riots, the fall of the government and a record default on the national debt.

In the 1990s the peso was fixed one to one to the dollar, which ended hyperinflation but made exports costly and left the country dependent on foreign loans. When a recession began in 1998, debts grew. In December 2001 the government froze bank accounts, a measure called the corralito. Riots and looting broke out, over thirty people were killed, and President Fernando de la Rúa fled the presidential palace by helicopter. Argentina had five presidents in two weeks.

The government defaulted on about 100 billion dollars and ended the dollar link in 2002. Half the people fell into poverty. Recovery came under the Peronist Néstor Kirchner. Ecuador, in its own crisis of the same years, went the other way and adopted the dollar.
sum: The Argentine great depression of 1998 to 2002 was a deep economic crisis in Argentina that peaked in December 2001 with riots, the fall of the government and a record default on the national debt.
